driverFlowIntro: End-to-end flow for drivers in WERET (demo). Follow the same order on every trip.
driverFlowStep1: Go online so your location is sent to the server and pending rides appear in the list.
driverFlowStep2: Accept a ride from the list — pickup and destination pins appear on the map with the route line.
driverFlowStep3: Drive to pickup; when the passenger is with you, tap Start trip. The passenger sees you as “ongoing” on their map.
driverFlowStep4: During the trip the map can show the passenger’s live position when they share location; follow the route to the drop-off.
driverFlowStep5: Tap End trip at the destination, then the passenger can rate you. Pull History to review completed rides.

WERET connects passengers and drivers with simple booking and live tracking.

This build is for development and demo. Features may change as we improve reliability and coverage.

featureNotificationsBody:
These switches apply on this device only (demo).

• Trip status updates
• Offers & news from WERET
featureRideTipsBody:
Follow these steps for a smooth booking:

• Allow location so WERET can center the map on you.
• First tap on the map sets pickup; second tap sets destination.
• Tap Request ride when both points are set and the map is not locked by an active trip.
• After a driver accepts, watch them approach on the map.
featureSafetyBody:
A few habits that keep every trip safer:

• Confirm pickup and destination pins before you start.
• Share live trip details with someone you trust while the ride is ongoing.
• Check that driver and vehicle details in the app match in real life.
• Use in-app actions to end the trip if something feels wrong.

weretGoogleApisConsole:
In Google Cloud:
• Google Auth Platform → Branding + Audience (Test users)
• Clients → Web client + Android client
• Do not add weret:// to the Web client — Android uses com.ridehail.app
weretGoogleDeveloperError:
Android setup in Google Cloud is wrong.
• Package: com.ridehail.app
• SHA-1 from debug.keystore (keytool)
• webClientId in .env must be the Web client ID
weretGoogleDevHint: If Google does not work, use Continue with phone.
weretGoogleExpoGoBlocked:
Google does not work in Expo Go (causes error 400).

Install the app on your phone:
cd mobile
npx expo run:android

Then open WERET from the home screen (not Expo Go).

Also check: Audience → Test users → the same Gmail you pick.
weretGoogleFirebaseLinkFailed: Could not link Google with Firebase. Enable Google in Firebase → Authentication and check Firebase keys in mobile/.env.
weretGoogleInitializing: Google sign-in is starting. Wait a moment and try again.
weretGoogleInvalidClient: Invalid client ID. Web ID in .env for the server; Android ID in EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID.
weretGoogleNoIdToken: Could not get a token from Google. Try again.
weretGoogleNotConfigured:
Google is not configured.
• backend/.env → GOOGLE_OAUTH_WEB_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_OAUTH_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID
• mobile/.env → EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID and EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID
• Restart the API and Expo
weretGooglePlayServices: Update Google Play Services from the Play Store, then try again.
weretGooglePolicyBlocked:
Google blocked sign-in (error 400).
1) Audience → Test users → add the same Gmail you select
2) Android client: com.ridehail.app + correct SHA-1 (from keytool)
3) Press r in Metro and try again
4) Or use Continue with phone
weretGoogleRebuildRequired:
For best results on Android, rebuild once:
cd mobile
npx expo run:android

Until then, try Google after adding Test users — it may work without a rebuild.
weretGoogleServerDisabled: Google is disabled on the server. Add GOOGLE_OAUTH_WEB_CLIENT_ID to backend/.env and restart the API.
weretGoogleSetupSteps:
One-time Google setup:
1) console.cloud.google.com → Google Auth Platform → Branding (app name + email)
2) Audience → External → Testing → Test users → add the Gmail you will sign in with
3) Clients → Web + Android (package com.ridehail.app + SHA-1 from keytool)
4) Copy client IDs to backend/.env and mobile/.env
5) Restart API and press r in Metro
weretGoogleSoonBody: Check Google Cloud setup (test users + Android client) and try again, or use Continue with phone.
